Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 7; Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r 3; Civil Code of Québec, arts 2236-2269 (société en commandite)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of each partner's passport and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary / Commissioner for oaths in jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via designated Canadian or foreign competent authority; consular legalization only where apostille is not recognized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency or equivalent legal existence certificate for corporate partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus certified translation into French if issued in English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / compliance certificate for non-resident corporate partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Revenue or corporate registry authority of partner's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) executed in notarized form
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization within Quebec; foreign authentication only if executed abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership declaration for each natural person owning 25% or more of the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partner and each disclosing UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized declaration; apostille or consular legalization for foreign signatories

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general and limited partners, UBOs, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Canadian Special Economic Measures Act sanctions lists, and Interpol/domestic law enforcement watchlists; mandatory identification and enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign) under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC Guidance; CIP/KYC documentation preserved for at least five years after termination of business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Revenu Québec / Registraire d'entreprise) - https://www.registrairedesentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The business name must be in French or have a French version registered; permitted English terms may be used with a French version; the name must not be contrary to public order and must not be misleading; for a société en commandite, the registered name must include the words 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' where the name is in French, or the equivalent English designation 'limited partnership' / 'L.P.' if used as the secondary language version; foreign-script names must be transliterated into Latin characters for registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Université / collège / école (unless educational authorization obtained)
Gouvernement / Canada / Québec (when used to imply sovereign sponsorship)
Oil / pétrole / mining (when implying regulated activities)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name reservation is refused, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request to the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of refusal, accompanied by a revised name and supporting explanatory submissions under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; if the Registraire maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Court of Québec (division of small claims / civil division) within 30 days of the reconsideration decision, and may file a new reservation for an alternate name in parallel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are generally accepted for a limited partnership's registered head office only if the provider operates a physical establishment in Quebec, maintains normal business hours, accepts service of legal process, and the partnership separately maintains substantive production/operational premises; a mail-forwarding-only or PO Box address will not satisfy Quebec substantiation requirements and will increase audit risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-Low ~10% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Registraire or a CRA/Revenu Québec verification visit; the inspection probability rises to the 20-25% range for the first fiscal year when the registered office differs from the principal production location.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of notarized limited partnership agreement and certificate of partnership
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Quebec professional hourly/fixed-fee benchmark for cross-border limited partnerships

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/AML/PEP/sanctions screening of all partners and beneficial owners via FINTRAC-compliant compliance platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance data provider (e.g., Refinitiv / Dow Jones / World-Check)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription/per-screen benchmark for low-risk standard screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization of notarized partner documents and certified translations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Global Affairs Canada / delegated competent authority / courier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government processing fee (approximately CAD 50 per document) plus commercial courier/translation costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market annual retainer for Quebec registered office plus service-of-process handling

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991) arts. 2236-2274 governing the société en commandite; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1) ss. 7, 14 and 62; Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1) ss. 29-35; Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) art. 28 for corporate-name compliance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Quebec Enterprise Registrar — electronic register at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership) filed by the general partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account mandated for a Quebec société en commandite. Under CCQ arts. 2243-2245, each limited partner's contribution must be fixed in the partnership contract and actually transferred to the partnership; the Declaration of Registration must state the total amount of contributions at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the board of directors of [GP Manager Inc.], general partner of [LP Name], société en commandite governed by the Civil Code of Quebec (arts. 2236 et seq.), approves the partnership agreement and the subscription of the capital contributions of the general and limited partners as set forth therein. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the registered office (siège social) of the Partnership be established at [Address], Province of Quebec, and that the Partnership's Declaration of Registration be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (c. P-44.1). RESOLVED FURTHER: That [Name] be appointed Chief Manager and [Name] be appointed Secretary, each authorized to execute registrations, banking, tax, licensing and operational instruments for the Partnership. This resolution is effective upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Société en Commandite Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal drafting — executed before a Quebec lawyer or notary; no government window involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership contract under CCQ arts. 2236-2244 specifying name, Quebec domicile, object, duration, contributions and profit-sharing of the general and limited partners. Where the general partner is a corporation, annex its act of incorporation and current attestation. Execute signature pages; notarization is optional unless immovables are contributed.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all general and limited partners
Certificate of incorporation and attestation of corporate general partner
Proposed partnership name and object clause
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Not applicable at this private step; if counsel identifies defects, amend and re-execute the agreement by private writing before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Legal Form Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a confusion/direct-hit search in the REQ register and verify compliance of the proposed French-language designation with art. 28 of the Charter of the French Language. If the name is found distinctive, proceed directly to the declaration, or use the REQ reservation service to secure the name before filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed French or bilingual corporate designation
REQ online access code (clé d'accès) or card payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search flags confusion or a prohibited expression, file an alternative name; on a formal rejection, resubmit within 30 days or request administrative review of the REQ decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Declaration of Registration and Obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — electronic filing portal at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite with the partnership name, Quebec registered-office address, complete identification of the general partner(s), total amount of contributions paid, and the e-mail for service of notices. Attach the executed partnership agreement abstract; pay the CA$40 registration fee; accept electronic publication. The REQ assigns the NEQ and issues the Certificate of Registration immediately, or within 5 business days if manual review is triggered.
required_dossiers: Attestation of the corporate general partner's existence
Proof of registered office address in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a défaut (query) notice, file a corrective declaration within the prescribed period (normally 30 days); if the file is refused, re-submit with corrected statements and request administrative review before the REQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax File Registration — GST/HST, QST and Payroll Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec for QST and statutory deductions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the Business Number (BN) and register the limited partnership for GST/HST (5%) and QST (9.975%) once taxable streaming-app revenue is generated; identify the mandate-holder (managing general partner) to Revenu Québec and open the QST, payroll deductions and employer contributions files using the NEQ. Confirm applicability of the digital-services GST/HST registration framework for in-app revenues.
required_dossiers: Estimated annual Canadian and Quebec taxable revenue
Apple IAP / Google Play / Stripe merchant identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is queried or left pending, resubmit through the CRA/Revenu Québec portals furnishing the missing attestations within 30 days; request rectification of registration dates to avoid late-filing penalties.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and income tax, and Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and Quebec income tax. Primary portals: CRA Business Registration Online and My Business Account at canada.ca; Revenu Québec's Entreprises Québec portal and CléNumérique at revenuquebec.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) is fiscally transparent and does not itself pay income tax, but it must establish a federal Business Number (BN) with CRA using Form RC1 (Partnership Registration) or online Business Registration Online, and must open a GST/HST account if it exceeds the small supplier threshold. The LP must also register with Revenu Québec for QST using Form LM-1 or online registration, providing the partnership declaration, list of general and limited partners, and Quebec place of business details. Each partner must supply its own tax identifier: Canadian partners use SIN/BN; non-resident partners must supply a tax identification number from their country of residence and, if carrying on a taxable activity in Canada, obtain a CRA non-resident account number. A foreign partner with no Canadian presence may need to appoint a representative for service of process and file prescribed withholding elections under the Income Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no general check-the-box or entity-classification election; the Quebec LP is classified as fiscally transparent by operation of ITA sections 96-103 and the Quebec Taxation Act. There is no election to convert the LP into an entity taxed at partnership level. The principal elections relevant to an LP are: (i) an election under ITA subsection 34(1) for an alternative taxation year of the partnership; (ii) partner-level elections affecting allocation and at-risk loss limitations under ITA subsection 96(2.1) and related provisions; and (iii) GST/HST partnership registration elections under the Excise Tax Act where the partnership is treated as a registrant for the purposes of the joint venture. If a non-Canadian member is itself a hybrid entity, Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules (ITA sections 18.2 et seq.) may automatically disallow or adjust mismatching tax outcomes; such rules do not provide a unilateral statutory election to alter the LP's Canadian classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax at 5%) and QST (Quebec provincial value-added tax at 9.975%)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in total worldwide taxable supplies, other than supplies of capital assets, measured in the current calendar quarter and in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters for GST/HST; a similar CAD 30,000 threshold applies under the QST regime for taxable supplies made in Québec, with mandatory registration once the threshold is exceeded or the registrant is a non-resident carrying on a commercial activity in Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Québec do not impose real-time fiscal clearance, pre-invoice digital stamping, or mandatory continuous transaction controls. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically through CRA GST/HST NETFILE or a CRA-approved API/EDI channel when the registrant exceeds prescribed electronic filing thresholds. QST returns must be filed electronically through Revenu Québec's e-services. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary and may be exchanged through Peppol-compatible networks, but no government validation, serialization, or clearance is required before issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act for: (i) tangible personal property exported by the supplier, delivered to a carrier for export, or exported in the course of a continuous journey; (ii) services supplied to a non-resident person where the service is performed outside Canada and is not in respect of Canadian real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada; and (iii) intangible personal property, including streaming licences and digital intellectual-property rights, supplied to a non-resident person where the property is not used in Canada and is not a prescribed supply made through a Canadian establishment. For a vertical micro-drama distribution business through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing, the LP's supplies to the app-store operator or to non-resident end users may be zero-rated when the records demonstrate that the digital content is delivered outside Canada, the contracting recipient is non-resident, and the supply is not part of the seller's Canadian business establishment. The seller must retain contemporaneous evidence of non-residency and place of consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Customs Coding Form B13A) or authorized e-manifest data for physical export shipments
Commercial invoice and signed contract identifying the non-resident purchaser or app-store operator
Bill of lading, air waybill, or carrier manifest evidencing physical exportation
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT or bank credit advice evidencing payment from outside Canada
Streaming royalty reports, user-geolocation logs, and platform settlement reports substantiating digital delivery to non-resident consumers
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess beyond the normal four-year limitation period where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established, and may claw back zero-rating together with unremitted GST/HST and QST, interest, and penalties. Penalties include gross-negligence penalties under section 285.1 of the Excise Tax Act (up to 50% of the misreported net tax), failure-to-remit penalties and daily interest, and Quebec penalties under the Taxation Act and the Act respecting the Québec Sales Tax. Deliberate fraudulent export claims can lead to criminal prosecution with fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with prudential oversight by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); no separate exchange-control authority or Foreign Exchange Administration mandate exists in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely convertible under both the current and capital accounts. There are no exchange controls, no registration or approval requirements for cross-border fund transfers, and no limits on profit or dividend remittances to non-resident partners. Quebec is subject to the federal Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act for the LP's general partner, but the LP's capital account and partnership income allocations may be repatriated freely. Horizontal taxation issues do not apply; remittance is a cash distribution from the LP, subject to the LP's partnership agreement and Quebec's Civil Code obligations. Non-resident partners may receive distributions without Bank of Canada approval; the only applicable compliance is Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Part XIII withholding tax on certain amounts, with treaty relief available under the Canada-US Tax Treaty for U.S. partners, and under other applicable treaties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation, or conversion ratio for export receipts. A Quebec limited partnership earning revenue from global vertical micro-drama distribution (via Apple IAP, Google Play, Stripe) may retain ad revenues in foreign currency (USD/EUR) in offshore or deemed-foreign settlement accounts; however, for CRA reporting, all income must be reported annually in CAD using the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate or an acceptable average rate. No statutory timeline exists for converting export proceeds into CAD.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Canada does not grant a distinct 'electronic money institution' (EMI) license comparable to EU EMI passports. Payment service providers in Quebec require either a bank license under the Bank Act, a provincial money-services licence (in Quebec, registration with the Autorité des marchés financiers for money services businesses under the Money-Services Businesses Act), or an agent/white-label arrangement with a Schedule I bank. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK/FCA EMIs) cannot isolate the LP from Canadian AML compliance; they may provide USD settlement rails for Stripe or platform proceeds, but funds flowing into a Canadian LP bank account must be routed through a regulated Canadian financial institution. Effective practical rating: Medium for multi-currency treasury holding, Low for accepting regulated settlement without a Canadian banking partner.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement for physical presence at a branch for all federal banks, but most Canadian Schedule I banks require at least one general partner or authorized signatory to complete an in-person or video-call identity verification (hybrid onboarding). Remote opening is generally permitted if digital KYC (ID scan, biometric liveness, and proof of address) meets Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) requirements and the bank's internal risk policy. For Quebec, National Bank and Desjardins may require a physical or notarized signature for a limited partnership account because the LP must demonstrate valid registration under the Quebec Enterprise Registrar (Registraire des entreprises). Recommended approach: complete a video interview with a corporate banking officer and use an electronic signature via a bank-approved platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity inherent in a limited partnership structure (multiple limited partners, nominee agreements, or foreign-held LP interests).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Certified LP agreement and certificate of registration from the Quebec Enterprise Registrar; (ii) a complete beneficial-ownership register listing every partner above the 10% threshold, with legal name, date of birth, country of tax residence, and source of wealth declaration; (iii) sworn statutory declarations from the general partner confirming no undisclosed trusts or acting nominees; (iv) clear delegation of signatory authority to the general partner's directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual high-volume cross-border transactions from streaming-platform clearing accounts (Apple IAP, Google Play) without a documented 'source of funds' chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Signed distribution agreements with platform operators; (ii) app-store analytics dashboards showing content title-level transaction detail; (iii) monthly payout statements from Apple/Google/Stripe reconciled to bank deposits; (iv) transfer pricing/file documentation for intercompany IP royalties; (v) a standard operating policy requiring transaction-level justification for all inbound credits, with originator legal entity and purpose code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction counterparties (e.g., app users in China, Russia, or other monitored states) filtering through digital EMI wallets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Enhanced due-diligence questionnaire for each recurring counterparty; (ii) geoblocking logs and device/IP analytics demonstrating compliance with export-control and sanctions rules; (iii) customer-contract terms excluding sanctioned territories; (iv) bank reference letters from the Canadian principal bank; (v) a sanctions screening audit report from a FINTRAC-registered compliance consultant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Income tax or withholding tax discrepancies from the LP's passthrough classification, triggering bank suspicion of criminal proceeds or unreported foreign assets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) CRA TP1 Partnership Information Return and Partner Allocation Schedule; (ii) T2-to-TP1 reconciliation; (iii) U.S. Schedule K-1 if any U.S. limited partner exists, showing no unreported share; (iv) CRA Notice of Assessment for the partnership and major partners; (v) a certified statement from the LP's tax accountant identifying the default pass-through tax classification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For compliant injection of capital into the Quebec LP, route via SWIFT MT103 payments from each limited partner's home jurisdiction. Use a clear purpose code — e.g., 'EQUI' (equity injection) for a capital contribution, or 'DEBT/GIFT' only if backed by a genuine loan/deed of contribution. The wire should reference the LP's corporate name and the specific capital account code shown in the Quebec Enterprise Registrar. The bank will require a copy of the signed limited partnership agreement and a resolution from the general partner authorizing the capital call. No Canadian exchange control approval is needed; however, circuits must pass through a sanctioned-party screening system (UN/OSFI), and each wire must identify the ultimate funding source. For escrow-held capital, maintain separate Capital Escrow Account at National Bank or RBC and only release into the operational account after a partner consent notice to the general partner.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements (payments to content production studios, professional actors, licensing houses, or platform commission fees) should be executed using: (i) domestic EFT (the Canadian Large Value Transfer System — LVTS) for CAD operations; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border USD/EUR trade settlement, with standard fields 50F and 59 identifying legal entities; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit only where physical goods or services require documentary assurance, which is uncommon for digital intellectual-property disbursements; (iv) Stripe Connect payout rails for global app-store disbursements to contractors, provided the recipient and transaction are subject to the same AML monitoring as wire transfers. Keep a full audit trail of purchase orders, invoices, and platform settlement statements to satisfy the bank's trade-payment due diligence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for multi-year production financing
Rolling spot contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank (non-speculative, transaction-linked)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally not necessary or permissible for CAD quotations due to full convertibility, but an NDF referencing USD/CAD is technically permitted under OSFI market-risk guidelines if used solely for hedge effectiveness and documented against underlying receivables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update declaration (declaration de mise a jour annuelle) under An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between the 1st day of the calendar month preceding the registration anniversary and the last day of the calendar month containing the anniversary of the initial REQ registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a registrar default notice; continued non-compliance may result in administrative strike-off from the REQ, loss of legal publicity protection, and fines under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) and T5013 Summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership fiscal period end; for a December 31 fiscal period, due by May 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to Income Tax Act penalties on a per-day, per-partner basis; continued default may lead to CRA arbitrary assessment, daily penalty accumulation, and prosecution for willful non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership information return and partner slips (TP-600 and RL-15, as applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership fiscal period end, generally aligned with the federal T5013 due date; partner slips due in accordance with Revenu Quebec annual filing rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or issue slips may result in Revenu Quebec fixed and daily penalties, interest on unreported amounts, and demand letters or tax assessments against the partnership and its general partner.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit is imposed by Quebec law or CRA on a private micro limited partnership solely because of its legal form. A statutory or contractual audit may become mandatory if the partnership agreement so requires, if a limited partner exercises certain statutory rights under the Civil Code of Quebec, if the LP is a reporting issuer or investment fund under securities law, or if the LP has been accepted as a public business enterprise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For a private Quebec limited partnership, the applicable domestic framework is Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook. IFRS is required only if the partnership is publicly accountable, a reporting issuer, or has otherwise elected or been required to follow IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation return on limited partnerships. The annual REQ declaration confirms the LP's public registration particulars, but limited partners are not generally named in the public registry. Partnership interests, not shares, are transferred; such transfers are recorded internally and reflected by an amended REQ declaration only when they affect required legal publicity details such as the general partner. No annual share-transfer confirmation is required because share structure does not exist.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (capital accounts and partnership-interest percentages)
Legal Publicity Dossier (all REQ declarations, amendments, and registration certificate)
Minute Book of the General Partner (management resolutions and partnership decisions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110-335 equivalent (CAD 150-450) per year for registered office or authorized agent services in Quebec, depending on city and service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500-5,000 for a small pass-through limited partnership if an audit becomes contractually or statutorily required; no statutory audit fee applies to the default micro LP scenario
